findings.title: Retry count is not persisted before nack, so poison messages can loop forever instead of reaching the DLQ
findings.evidence: The worker computes 'attempts = _delivery_attempts(message) + 1' and on failure below the threshold immediately calls 'queue.nack(message)' without updating the message attributes. Since '_delivery_attempts' reads from 'message.attributes', a broker that redelivers the same message unchanged will keep returning 0 and the code will stay on the retry branch forever.
findings.recommendation: Do not rely on mutating local state for retry counting. Persist the incremented attempt count in broker-supported metadata before requeueing, or use a broker-provided delivery/redelivery counter instead of 'message.attributes'. If neither is available, republish the message with updated attributes and ack the original only after the republish succeeds.
